args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing production health checks immediately after deploy v2.3.1 reached all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west); error rate rose to ~18%. Investigation: release history showed v2.3.1 as unhealthy in production, with v2.3.0 the most recent healthy production release (v2.2.9 also healthy; v2.3.1-rc was staging-only and also unhealthy).

Action taken: rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0 in all production regions. The first rollback attempt halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed state (us-east v2.3.0, us-west/eu-west v2.3.1). The rollback was retried and completed; all three regions now report v2.3.0 with healthy=true and error rate ~0.2%.

Follow-up: determine root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before any redeploy. Note this was a rollback to a previously-healthy version, so no change-manager approval was required.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident did go through despite the timeout, so no retry was needed.

## Summary

**Done — checkout-api is recovered.**

1. **Diagnosis:** `get_service_status` showed checkout-api on v2.3.1 in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), `healthy: false`, error rate 18%. Release history confirmed v2.3.1 as `unhealthy` in production. The most recent **healthy production** release was **v2.3.0** (v2.2.9 was healthy but older; v2.3.1-rc was staging-only *and* unhealthy, so not a candidate).

2. **Rollback to v2.3.0:**
   - First attempt failed partway: `partial_failure: Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error`, leaving a mixed state (us-east v2.3.0, us-west/eu-west v2.3.1).
   - Retried the same rollback; it completed: all three regions on v2.3.0, `status: rolled_out`.
   - Verified post-rollback: `healthy: true`, error rate **0.2%**.

3. **Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2 on checkout-api, documenting the v2.3.1 failure, the partial-then-completed rollback, and the current healthy state. The `create_incident` call timed out at 30s, so I checked `list_incidents` rather than blindly retrying — the incident had in fact been created (single copy, no duplicate).

**Policy note:** This was a rollback to a version that had previously been healthy in production, so change-manager approval was not required. If the intent is to redeploy v2.3.1, that *would* require change-manager approval since v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production — root cause should be found first.
